rows.q: Year the hematology service and the HSCT program were established
International accreditation: JCI, JACIE (FACT-JACIE), FACT — for which programs (HSCT, cell therapy), validity period
Membership in EBMT / CIBMTR / APBMT; does the hospital report data to the registry
Participation in hematology clinical trials: active trials, phases, are foreign patients enrolled
Hematology and HSCT publications over the past 5 years, leading specialists (full name, area of expertise)
AML: number of new patients per year (adults / children)
ALL, including Ph+: number of new patients per year (adults / children)
MDS, CMML: number of patients per year
CML, Ph-negative MPN, myelofibrosis: number of patients per year
Lymphomas: Hodgkin lymphoma, aggressive and indolent NHL, T-cell lymphomas, primary CNS lymphomas — number of patients per year
Multiple myeloma, AL amyloidosis: number of patients per year
Aplastic anemia, PNH: number of patients, availability of IST (ATG) and complement inhibitors
Hemoglobinopathies (thalassemia, sickle cell anemia): experience with HSCT and other treatment methods
Hemophilia and other coagulopathies, including those with inhibitors; orthopedic surgery in patients with hemophilia
Primary immunodeficiencies, histiocytoses, inherited bone marrow failure syndromes
Pediatric hematology and HSCT: is there a pediatric unit, from what age are patients accepted, number of pediatric HSCTs per year
Total HSCTs per year over the last 3 years (auto / allo)
Allo-HSCT from an HLA-identical related donor: number per year
Allo-HSCT from an unrelated donor: number per year
Haploidentical HSCT: number per year, approach (post-transplant cyclophosphamide, TCRαβ/CD19 depletion)
Cord blood transplantation: do you perform it, number per year
Auto-HSCT: number per year, for which diseases; tandem HSCT for myeloma
Age limits for auto- and allo-HSCT; reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC) regimens for older patients
Eligibility criteria for HSCT: disease status (remission, MRD), comorbidity (HCT-CI), ECOG; do you accept patients who are not in remission
Graft source (bone marrow / PBSC); who performs donor collection and where
GVHD prophylaxis: standard regimens (ATG, cyclophosphamide, etc.), treatment of steroid-refractory GVHD (ruxolitinib, photopheresis)
Possibility of a second HSCT in case of relapse or graft failure
Access to donor registries: which ones (WMDA, DKMS, national)
Average time from search initiation to unrelated-donor HSCT
HLA typing of the patient and relatives: do you accept typing performed in Kazakhstan; what resolution and which loci are required
Requirements for a related donor: work-up (can it be done on our side), travel, length of stay, age
Transplant-related mortality (NRM/TRM) at day 100 and at 1 year: auto / allo related / unrelated / haplo
Overall survival (OS) and relapse-free survival at 1 and 3 years after allo-HSCT for the main diseases
Relapse rate after allo-HSCT; post-transplant maintenance therapy
Incidence of grade II–IV and III–IV acute GVHD, chronic GVHD
Incidence of graft failure and graft rejection; time to engraftment
Induction outcomes in AML and ALL (complete remission rate, MRD negativity), early mortality
Source of outcome data (internal registry, EBMT/CIBMTR report, publications) and the years covered
CAR-T: is it available; which products (commercial, manufactured in-house, within clinical trials); for which indications (B-ALL, DLBCL, myeloma, etc.)
CAR-T: number of procedures per year, time from apheresis to infusion, incidence of grade III–IV CRS and ICANS
Bispecific antibodies (blinatumomab, teclistamab, glofitamab, epcoritamab, etc.) and antibody–drug conjugates (inotuzumab, etc.)
Targeted therapy (FLT3, IDH, BCL2, menin, BTK inhibitors, etc.): availability and regulatory approval in your country
Donor lymphocyte infusions (DLI), virus-specific T cells, extracorporeal photopheresis
Gene therapy (thalassemia, sickle cell anemia, hemophilia)
MRD: flow cytometry (sensitivity, number of colors), PCR-MRD, NGS-MRD; at which time points after HSCT
Molecular genetics: NGS panels for myeloid and lymphoid neoplasms, turnaround time
Cytogenetics and FISH: panels, turnaround time
Chimerism monitoring: method (STR, qPCR, NGS), sensitivity, schedule
Histology and IHC review: is it mandatory; do you accept digital slides and our blocks/slides
Which of our test results do you accept without repeating them, and how recent must they be
PET-CT, MRI: availability and waiting times
Number of hematology and HSCT beds; isolation rooms with HEPA filtration and positive pressure
ICU experienced in managing hematology patients; dialysis, mechanical ventilation, ECMO in the same building
24/7 on-call hematologist / transplant physician service; nurse-to-patient ratio in the HSCT unit
Transfusion medicine: irradiated and leukoreduced components, platelet availability, are donors from the patient's family required
Apheresis, cryobank, cell processing laboratory

Infection control: infectious disease specialist, local antimicrobial resistance patterns, incidence of invasive fungal infections; availability of antifungal and antiviral drugs (posaconazole, letermovir, etc.)
Supportive services: psychologist, nutritionist, rehabilitation, palliative care, fertility preservation
Full name, city, country; type of hospital (public, private, university)
National status (reference center, center of competence, etc.)
Willingness to consult on de-identified data (without full name, IIN (individual identification number), date of birth) and on digital slides without personal labeling
Response time for a de-identified request: preliminary treatment plan and cost estimate
Online case conferences with our physicians: are they possible, language, who participates on the hospital's side, cost
Time from patient consent to admission; is there a waiting list for HSCT / CAR-T
Willingness to agree on the division of treatment phases: what we do in Kazakhstan before departure (induction, additional work-up) and after return
Discharge summary and discharge recommendations: language, timing, format; do they include the conditioning protocol, doses, follow-up plan
Communication after return: teleconsultations for our physicians, cost, response time; who makes decisions in case of relapse or GVHD
Procedure for complications after return: on-call physician contact, possibility of readmission and its terms
Russian-speaking coordinator or interpreter for the patient; languages spoken by physicians
List of documents required from the patient for admission: language, is a certified translation required
Experience with patients from Kazakhstan and the CIS: number per year, diseases
Average length of stay: inpatient and outpatient phase near the hospital (auto-HSCT, allo-HSCT, CAR-T)
Is the patient required to stay near the hospital after discharge (until day 100, etc.); can the patient return earlier under our follow-up
Accommodation near the hospital: does the hospital assist, monthly cost, housing requirements after HSCT
Visa support (invitation letter) for the patient, donor and accompanying persons; processing times
How many accompanying persons are allowed and needed; requirements for them
Travel: direct flights from Astana / Almaty, travel time; arrangement of medical transport for a critically ill patient
Has a memorandum been signed with our Center, its term, are there confidentiality obligations
Language of the contract with the patient, governing law, claims procedure
Hospital liability insurance toward the patient
Patient confidentiality and data protection policy
Contact person for our Center: full name, position, email, phone
Cost of unrelated donor search and activation, graft delivery
Package price for auto-HSCT (currency)
Package price for allo-HSCT: from a related / unrelated / haploidentical donor
Package price for CAR-T; cost of a course of induction chemotherapy
What is and is not included in the package: drugs, transfusions, ICU, tests, outpatient phase, readmissions
Policy when costs exceed the package: how charges are calculated, is the patient notified in advance, average actual bill for allo-HSCT
Cost per ICU day and of high-cost drugs (defibrotide, letermovir, ATG, ruxolitinib, etc.)
Deposit and prepayment, currency and payment methods, refund of unused funds
Installment plans, discounts, work with insurance companies and charitable foundations

sheets.title: 4. Information from the hospital: strengths and weaknesses

rows.q: In which areas of hematology and HSCT does the hospital consider itself a leader in the country / region
Unique technologies, programs or drugs not available at most centers
For which patient categories (disease, age, disease status) is the hospital the most preferable choice, and why
Which patients does the hospital not accept or accept with restrictions (age, disease status, active infections, comorbidity)
Weaknesses and limitations the patient should know about in advance (waiting lists, language barrier, unavailable treatments or drugs)
Which of its advantages does the hospital consider most important for patients from Kazakhstan
